key_insight: A digital twin can test local collective tariffs in realistic distribution-level energy communities by combining household behavior, shared metering, and tariff logic in one simulation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to evaluate tariff designs for cost allocation, peak reduction, and regulatory fit in distribution-level energy systems with PV, batteries, and EVs.
method: Agent-based modeling of household load and generation
Explicit tariff rules embedded in a unified simulation environment
evidence_signal: The method was demonstrated on the Danish Local Collective Tariff across representative residential community scenarios, showing lower peak coincidence and measurable community-level cost reductions.
watch_item: Results depend on the timing match between consumption and generation, so cost neutrality may vary across participants and configurations.
paper_title: A Digital Twin-Based Method for Evaluating Local Collective Tariffs in Distribution-Level Energy Systems
